title: Tom Benton and alto horn in jazz bands
summary: Punch recalls a banjoist and how an alto horn player joined the jazz bands.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: What about Tom Benton? Did you ever work with him?
Yeah, he worked with him and Jack Carey Band. He was a banjo player.
Did they have many odd homemade instruments and stuff like that when you were coming up? No.

The only thing they used sometimes was a fellow could play a good alto, you know like playing brass band? Well they'd throw him in the jazz band if he could play it good, mixing that with us, you know.

Well they had a fellow Yard, forget that boy named him now, he used to play in most all these bands, that alto. Even him was Oscar. Oscar something. Oscar Devone, Oscar Devone, Oscar Devone, some kind of Oscar or nothing. But he could play that like that alto because he'd sit down and work with us lots of times. It helped out a whole lot. Like I said, we'd let you rest. Yeah. Did he play melody?
Well I'd take down when he'd play.
Yeah. He'd just swap, aren't you?
I'll tell you how he'd do, when we all opened up like that he'd play off, you know, play side melody, see. And then if I'd take down and say I'd jump on the lead, see.
Well that ought to sound pretty good. Sure it did. I've heard Ricard play a little melody on an alto horn sound pretty nice. I can't think of many of those guys like that I know.
No, that meant all these instruments come out here in Italy man. It worked out when I first started.
